cards.headline: Written with a crushed foot and a Stones record
cards.snippet: In 1991, Noel Gallagher was working for a building company in his hometown of Manchester when a pipe crushed his foot. He was moved to a lighter storeroom job, which gave him more time to write songs. One night he played a chord progression of his own over the Rolling Stones' album Exile on Main St. and found it fit a vocal melody from "Shine a Light". He reworked that melody into the line "Maybe I don't really want to know", which for a while was the only finished part of "Live Forever".

cards.headline: A reply to Nirvana's 'I Hate Myself and Want to Die'
cards.snippet: Noel Gallagher wrote "Live Forever" in the early 1990s, at the height of grunge. He disliked Nirvana's "I Hate Myself and Want to Die" and felt kids didn't need to hear that message. He has said the song was not a direct retort to Nirvana, and he is a fan of the band. He did contrast Kurt Cobain, who seemed to have everything and still be miserable, with his own band. They had almost nothing, yet he thought waking up each morning was great.
cards.context: Noel contrasted Cobain, who had everything and was miserable, with his own broke but happy band.

cards.headline: "I realized how much I love life"
cards.snippet: This song saved me from suicide 15 years ago. I heard it and I started to cry because I realized how much I love life.
cards.context: Fits the song's optimism, which Noel wrote as an answer to grunge nihilism.
